target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: Gateway: allow extension origins in browser allowlist
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` (strictly speaking this allows chrome extensions/electron+tauri apps to connect but I think calling it a new capability is a stretch) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: `N/A` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: local Bun + Vitest - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WS browser-origin client; Chrome extension origin emulated in handshake tests via `ws` - Relevant config (redacted): `gateway.auth.mode="token"`, `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]` ### Steps 1. Configure the Gateway with token auth and `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]`. 2. Open a WS connection that sends `Origin: chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop` and a valid `connect` request. 3. Observe the handshake result. ### Expected - An exactly allowlisted extension origin should be accepted, just like an exactly allowlisted `https://...` origin. ### Actual - Before this fix, the request was rejected with `origin not allowed` because the checker collapsed the extension origin to `"null"` internally. - After this fix, the handshake succeeds and returns `hello-ok`. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: whitelisted the chrome extension I'm developing and successfully connected to the Gateway via WS - Edge cases checked: N/A - What you did **not** verify: did not try with other protocols (`app://`, `tauri://`) ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` - If yes, exact upgrade steps: `N/A` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this commit; if extension access is urgently blocked, temporarily fall back to `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["*"]` until the regression is understood. - Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/origin-check.ts`; optionally restore prior `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` values in config. - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: an exactly allowlisted `chrome-extension://` still being rejected; malformed/non-matching non-standard origins unexpectedly being accepted; regressions in existing `http(s)` origin allowlisting.

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independently incorrect things:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** had a single-char logic bug (`!==` for `===`) that forced explicit completions config to Responses.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** shared the same predicate, but after model resolution the `api` field carries no provenance bit — per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config and catalog default `api: "openai-completions"` are identical strings. Need to inspect raw config to distinguish them.

The fix:

1. **`hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig()`** — checks BOTH `config.models.providers.openai.api` (provider-level) AND `config.models.providers.openai.models[].api` (per-model) to distinguish user intent from catalog defaults.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport()`** — rewritten with own catalog-normalization logic, decoupled from `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel`** — checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before normalizing. Returns model unchanged when user explicitly configured completions.

4. **`normalizeTransport`** — same check. Returns `undefined` (no override) when user explicitly configured completions.

## User Impact

Users who configure `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider level or on a specific model row now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — real production import exercising `buildOpenAIProvider()`:**

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs
[PASS] resolved: catalog → Responses: want=openai-responses got=openai-responses
[PASS] resolved: provider-level explicit completions: want=openai-completions got=openai-completions
[PASS] resolved: per-model explicit completions: want=openai-completions got=openai-completions
[PASS] transport: catalog → Responses: want=openai-responses got=openai-responses
[PASS] transport: provider explicit → undefined: want=undefined got=undefined
[PASS] transport: per-model explicit → undefined: want=undefined got=undefined

6/6 passed
```

The proof script imports `buildOpenAIProvider()` from the actual production module and exercises both `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks against all three config levels (catalog-default, provider-level, per-model).

**Test regression:**

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs
→ exit 0
```

**Observed result after fix:** All six scenarios pass. Per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config is now correctly distinguished from catalog defaults and respected by both `normalizeResolvedModel` (preserves `"openai-completions"` api) and `normalizeTransport` (returns `undefined`, no Responses override).

**What was not tested:** Real OpenAI API endpoint E2E. The proof exercises the exact callback functions the gateway calls; API key validity is a separate concern.

## Regression Test Plan

- `$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 45 tests passed**
- `$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts --run` — **2 passed, 246 tests passed**
- `$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs` — **exit 0**
- `$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs` — **6/6 passed**

## Root Cause

In `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`, `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` had a single-character logic error (`!==` for `===`) that inverted the explicit-config guard. Additionally, `normalizeOpenAITransport` shared the same predicate but the resolved model's `api` field has no provenance — a per-model user config and the catalog default are indistinguishable strings. The only way to separate them is to inspect the raw config, which the `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` helper now does.

target.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue
target.body:
Fixes #79589

## Problem

Upstream added priority scheduling (foreground/normal/background) via insertion-sort at enqueue time (#82765). Within a static priority tier, older background work can still sit behind later background work indefinitely when the lane stays busy.

## Fix

Implement a **foreground-preserving one-tier aging** policy:

- After `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30s), an entry is promoted by **exactly one priority tier** (`priority + 1`).
- Background (-1) ages to normal (0), still below fresh foreground (1).
- Fresh user/foreground work always runs before aged background.
- Aged background still beats fresh background at the same static priority.

This intentionally does **not** promote aged work to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` or above fresh foreground. The contract is fairness among same-or-lower tiers without starving interactive work.

Files:
- `lanes.ts`: export `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS`
- `command-queue.ts`: `effectivePriority()` (+1 after threshold) and `pickNextIndex()` (effective priority, then oldest enqueue time, then sequence)
- `command-queue.test.ts`: one-tier aging regression tests using `enqueueCommandInLane(CommandLane.Main, ...)`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Command-lane drain selects aged background before fresh background after 30s, while still preferring fresh foreground over aged background (one-tier aging).

**Real environment tested:** macOS, Node from the local OpenClaw checkout, branch `feat/command-queue-priority` at head `41cd18a776`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /tmp/oc-75299
node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
```

**Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched branch:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
 ✓ command queue > preserves foreground priority over aged background work
 ✓ command queue > promotes aged background above fresh background (one-tier starvation guard)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 30 skipped (32)
```

Source confirmation of the one-tier policy:

```console
$ grep -n "STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS\|return entry.priority" src/process/lanes.ts src/process/command-queue.ts
src/process/lanes.ts:15:export const STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS = 30_000;
src/process/command-queue.ts:282:  if (Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt >= STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS) {
src/process/command-queue.ts:283:    return entry.priority + 1;
src/process/command-queue.ts:285:  return entry.priority;
```

Behavioral contract exercised by the two tests:
1. Aged background then fresh foreground drain order: `["foreground", "background"]`
2. Aged background then fresh background drain order: `["aged-bg", "fresh-bg"]`

**Observed result after fix:** One-tier aging raises background to normal after 30s so it beats later background work, while fresh foreground still wins over aged background. Policy, comments, tests, and this proof describe the same contract.

**What was not tested:** Live gateway under wall-clock multi-session contention with real cron/foreground traffic.

target.title: fix: relay Claude CLI assistant partial messages as streaming deltas
target.body:
Fixes #86050

## Summary

Relay Claude CLI assistant records as streaming deltas so the WebChat UI shows progressive output instead of waiting for the full response.

**Fix 1**: Parse `assistant` records from the Claude CLI JSONL stream and forward their text content as `chat.delta` events.

**Fix 2**: Gate on `stop_reason` using a positive partial signal: only forward records where `stop_reason` is explicitly present and `null` (the documented Claude CLI partial marker). Complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped to avoid duplicating the final message. Records without `stop_reason` at all are ignored as ambiguous (could be complete messages from custom `claude-stream-json` backends).

## Changed files

- `src/agents/cli-output.ts` -- Added `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` with positive `stop_reason: null` guard
- `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` -- Tests covering partial forwarding, complete-message skip, absent-stop_reason rejection, and edge cases

## Verification

All tests use the documented `stop_reason: null` marker for partial messages:
- `stop_reason: null` (explicit) -> text forwarded as streaming delta
- `stop_reason: "end_turn"` -> record skipped (complete message, not a partial)
- `stop_reason` absent -> record skipped (not a confirmed partial; prevents false delivery from custom backends)
- Non-assistant record types -> ignored by the parser
- Malformed content arrays -> returns null without throwing
- Mixed text + tool_use content -> text extracted, tool_use entries ignored

Fixes #86050

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Claude CLI assistant records are not relayed as streaming deltas, so WebChat waits for the full response. The `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function requires a positive partial signal (`stop_reason: null` explicitly present) to skip complete messages and forward only true streaming partials as `chat.delta` events.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from branch `fix/gateway-stream-relay` at `/tmp/proof-86649`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Build from branch and verify the partial assistant delta parser is active in compiled production code.
Step 2. Feed four Claude CLI JSONL records through the production `createCliJsonlStreamingParser`: two partials (`stop_reason: null`), one complete (`stop_reason: "end_turn"`), and one ambiguous (no `stop_reason` field).

Evidence after fix: terminal output from the patched build:

The partial assistant delta parser and its `stop_reason: null` guard are active in the compiled production bundle:

```console
$ grep -n "parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta\|stop_reason.*null\|partialDelta" dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js
216:function parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta(params) {
220:if (!isRecord$1(message) || !("stop_reason" in message) || message.stop_reason !== null) return null;
394:const partialDelta = parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta({
402:if (partialDelta) {
403:assistantText = partialDelta.text;
404:params.onAssistantDelta(partialDelta);
```

Runtime exercise of the production parser with Claude CLI JSONL event shapes:

```console
$ npx tsx proof-exercise.ts
=== Feeding Claude CLI JSONL records through production parser ===

Input record 1 (partial, stop_reason: null):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"}]

Input record 2 (partial, stop_reason: null, extended text):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]

Input record 3 (complete, stop_reason: "end_turn"):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer to your question."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Complete message skipped (no new delta), avoiding duplicate delivery

Input record 4 (no stop_reason field, ambiguous source):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Some response"}]},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Record without stop_reason skipped (not a confirmed partial)

=== Summary ===
Total records fed: 4
Partial deltas relayed: 2
Delta breakdown:
  [0] delta="Here is" (cumulative: "Here is")
  [1] delta=" the answer" (cumulative: "Here is the answer")

Before fix: Records 1-2 would not emit deltas (assistant type was ignored).
After fix: Records 1-2 relay as streaming deltas. Records 3-4 correctly skipped.
No duplicate final text delivered.
```

Observed result after fix: The compiled production code at `dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js:216-220` contains the `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function with the positive partial signal guard (`stop_reason !== null`). At line 394, the main parser calls this function as a fallback when no raw stream delta is available. Runtime exercise confirms: assistant records with `stop_reason: null` relay as incremental streaming deltas (`"Here is"` then `" the answer"`), complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped (preventing duplicate delivery), and ambiguous records without `stop_reason` are also skipped (preventing false delivery from custom backends).

What was not tested: Live Claude CLI session with real streaming output over the gateway WebSocket connection. The fix exercises the production parser against the documented Claude CLI JSONL protocol shapes. End-to-end WebChat/TUI display was not verified.

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: route assistant-record partials through commentary classification.

- When classification is active, partial assistant text buffers into `pendingClaudeText` like stream_event text
- Assistant partials that include `tool_use` flush pending narration to `onCommentaryText`
- Regression: pre-tool partial text no longer lands on final assistant deltas

Terminal confirmation:

target.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization
target.body:
Fixes #90010
Fixes #79588

## Summary

Improve compaction identifier survival with transcript-wide extraction and quality-guard retry hints. Fixes two security/correctness issues found during review:

**Fix 1 — Sanitize string-encoded JSON arguments before extraction**: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` now parses string-encoded tool arguments as JSON and passes the parsed object through `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before identifier scanning. Previously, string arguments (e.g. OpenAI's JSON-stringified format) were appended raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`.

**Fix 2 — Fail strict compaction when cap recovery cannot fit**: When strict mode detects that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, compaction is now cancelled instead of returning a summary with known identifier loss. This prevents the session from continuing in a state where strict-required identifiers are silently dropped.

## Changed files

- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts` — Parse string args as JSON, sanitize via `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before appending; non-JSON strings still pass through
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` — Cancel compaction (return `{ cancel: true }` with reason) when strict cap recovery overflows instead of silently skipping
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` — Three regression tests: string-encoded JSON credential sanitization, non-JSON passthrough, strict-mode cap overflow cancel

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Two security/correctness issues in compaction identifier survival. (1) `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` appended string-encoded tool arguments raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`. (2) When strict mode detected that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, the summary was returned with known identifier loss instead of cancelling compaction.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5 arm64, Node v22.19.0, pnpm v11.2.2. Built from source on branch `compaction-identifier-survival-validation` at `/tmp/wt-75336`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Create proof script exercising production `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers`, `extractOpaqueIdentifiers`, `extractIdentifiersFromMessages`, `computeLostIdentifiers`, and `capCompactionSummary`:

```typescript
import {
  extractMessageTextForIdentifiers,
  extractOpaqueIdentifiers,
  extractIdentifiersFromMessages,
  computeLostIdentifiers,
} from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.js";
import { testing } from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.js";
const { capCompactionSummary, MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS } = testing;
```

Step 2. Validate Fix 1, string-encoded JSON args with credential `token` field:

```typescript
const msg = {
  role: "assistant",
  content: [{
    type: "functionCall", id: "call_1", name: "configure",
    arguments: '{"token":"deadbeef12345678","endpoint":"https://api.acme.io/v2"}',
  }],
};
const text = extractMessageTextForIdentifiers(msg);
assert(!text.includes("deadbeef12345678"));    // credential redacted
assert(text.includes("https://api.acme.io/v2")); // non-credential survives
```

Step 3. Validate Fix 2, capping loses identifiers and recovery overflows:

```typescript
const transcriptIds = extractIdentifiersFromMessages([
  { role: "user", content: "deploy hash a1b2c3d4e5f6" },
]);
const oversized = "## Decisions\nKeep flow.\n## Exact identifiers\n"
  + "x".repeat(MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS) + "\na1b2c3d4e5f6";
const capped = capCompactionSummary(oversized);
const lost = computeLostIdentifiers(transcriptIds, capped);
assert(lost.length > 0);  // identifier at tail truncated by capping
const recovered = `${capped}\n\n## Exact identifiers (recovered)\n- ${lost[0]}`;
assert(recovered.length > MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS); // recovery overflows
```

Step 4. Run `npx tsx proof-75336.ts` from the patched branch.

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ cd /tmp/wt-75336 && npx tsx proof-75336.ts

[Proof 1] String-encoded JSON args sanitization
  PASS credential token value is redacted from string args
  PASS non-credential endpoint survives sanitization
  PASS hex identifier extractor does not capture redacted credential
  PASS non-JSON string args pass through for extraction

[Proof 2] Identifier loss detection after capping
  PASS transcript identifiers extracted from messages
  PASS hex identifier normalized to uppercase
  PASS capped summary respects size limit
  PASS identifier at tail is lost after capping
  PASS recovery block exceeds cap (triggers cancel in strict mode)

Results: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Observed result after fix:

Fix 1: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` no longer leaks credential-field values from string-encoded JSON arguments. The `token` field value `deadbeef12345678` is redacted by `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before the hex identifier extractor can capture it. Non-credential fields and non-JSON strings pass through normally.

Fix 2: When strict mode detects identifier loss after capping and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000 chars), compaction is cancelled with a diagnostic reason instead of returning a summary with known missing identifiers. The cancel reason is stored via `setCompactionSafeguardCancelReason` for downstream diagnostics.

What was not tested: Live compaction with a real model and conversation history (requires a running OpenClaw session with enough context to trigger compaction).

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1s:

1. Gate post-cap strict identifier recovery/cancel on `qualityGuardEnabled` so `qualityGuard.enabled: false` keeps the opt-out.
2. Redact credential name/value shapes (`token: deadbeef...`) from non-JSON tool argument strings before identifier extraction.

Terminal confirmation:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts -t "redacts credential name|skips post-cap strict|cancels strict compaction when cap"
 ✓ redacts credential name/value shapes from non-JSON string arguments
 ✓ cancels strict compaction when cap recovery would exceed size limit
 ✓ skips post-cap strict identifier audit when qualityGuard is disabled

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (filtered)
```

Still not tested: live compaction run inside a full gateway session with real transcript volume.

target.title: fix(context): show transcript conversation in /context map
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/context map` rendered only static prompt composition from the cached run report: system prompt, workspace files, tool schemas, and skills. The conversation transcript, which is the part of context that grows between turns, had no treemap group, so the image and caption never changed between turns and did not represent actual context usage.

Release note: `/context map` now includes transcript conversation usage in the treemap and caption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Users expect the map to reflect current context usage as of the latest turn, consistent with the exact token totals that `/status` reports.

## User Impact

`/context map` on any channel now includes a Conversation group with User, Assistant, Tool results, Summaries, and Runtime context leaves. Transcript messages are sized with the embedded runner's own context estimator in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-char-estimator.ts`; the Runtime context leaf comes from `systemPromptReport.currentTurn.runtimeContextChars` because runtime context is injected transiently per turn (`installRuntimeContextMessageForPrompt` removes it after the prompt) and never reaches the transcript.

The caption now includes `Conversation: N chars (~M tok)`. The Current turn prompt tile is removed from `src/auto-reply/reply/context-treemap.ts`: the turn's prompt is persisted to the transcript on both normal and runtime-only turns, so the Conversation group already counts it and keeping the tile would double-count. `report.currentTurn` stays in the type and in `/context detail`. After compaction, conversation usage collapses into the Summaries leaf.

This is display-only. It adds no new persistence, config, or data collection, and reuses `readSessionMessages` plus `estimateMessageCharsCached` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-context-report.ts`.

## Evidence

Unit/typecheck:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/commands-context-report.test.ts`: 14/14 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: exit 0. `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: exit 0.

Real behavior proof (real setup): started the gateway from this branch against a state dir seeded with a real agent session (created by a real embedded model run, `source: "run"` report + transcript), then sent the command through the real webchat pipeline:

```
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"/context map", ...}'
{ "runId": "proof-ctx-map-1", "status": "started" }
```

target.title: fix(text): keep five src-side text truncations UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `src/`-side text-truncation call sites still use raw `String.prototype.slice()` (or template-string slicing) with no UTF-16 surrogate-pair awareness. When an emoji or other supplementary Unicode character lands exactly on the cap, the slice can leave a dangling high surrogate that downstream provider / prompt / log consumers may treat as malformed text.

| File | Site | Cap | Visibility |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `src/cli/plugins-list-format.ts:19` | `plugin.description` truncation in CLI row | 57 chars | user-facing terminal output |
| `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts:75` | `formatHookErrorForLog` truncation | `MAX_HOOK_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (500) | log line per hook failure |
| `src/auto-reply/fallback-state.ts:33` | `truncateFallbackReasonPart` for fallback reason text | 80 chars (configurable) | fallback notice surfaced in chat |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.ts:117` | `generateConversationLabel` output cap | `maxLength` (default 128) | short session label surfaced in UI |

Each follows the same pattern that has already landed in 30+ merged UTF-16 PRs (e.g. #102087, #102466, #102496, #102085, #102332, #102090, #102266, #102246, #102378, #102464, #102467, #102470, #102483, #102484, #102477).

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw `slice()` / `.slice(0, N)` patterns with `truncateUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` (re-exported via `src/utils.js`). The helper preserves the existing cap for ordinary text and only backs up by one code unit when the cap would split a surrogate pair — matching the contract every other UTF-16 fix in this wave uses.

The helper is the canonical one (already imported by `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts`, `src/talk/fast-context-runtime.ts`, `src/agents/bash-process-references.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/bash-command.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts`, etc.), so no new helper surface is added.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): use typed FailoverError.reason for rate_limit classification [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## Summary

Fixes issue #102598 where periodic usage-limit failures (e.g., "You've hit your weekly limit") were silently swallowed in group chats, leaving users with no visible error message.

## The Problem

When a provider account hits a periodic usage limit (weekly/monthly), the failover layer correctly classifies this as `FailoverError.reason = "rate_limit"`. However, the user-copy paths in `agent-runner-execution.ts` re-derived rate-limitedness from message text patterns using `isRateLimitErrorMessage(message)`, whose pattern list doesn't include "weekly limit" phrasing.

This caused periodic-limit failures to be misclassified as generic runner failures, which are intentionally silent in group chats per policy. Users saw a typing indicator followed by nothing - indistinguishable from a dead bot.

## What Changed

Two locations in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` (~1153, ~3453) now use the typed `FailoverError.reason` field for rate_limit/overloaded classification:

```typescript
const isRateLimit = isFailoverError(err)
  ? err.reason === "rate_limit" || err.reason === "overloaded"
  : isRateLimitErrorMessage(message); // fallback for non-FailoverError errors
```

This matches the existing pattern used for billing error classification at line ~3310-3314.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening (improves error visibility for auth/provider failures)

## Scope

- Auto-reply failure handling
- Group chat error visibility

## Linked Issue

Closes #102598

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

**Before**: Group chats show nothing when hitting weekly/monthly usage limits (silent failure)
**After**: Group chats surface the rate-limit error message from the provider, allowing users to understand what happened

## Security Impact

- **Does this change touch auth, sandbox, or secrets handling?** No
- **Does this change affect approval gates, exec policy, or tool permissions?** No
- **Does this change affect credential storage, transmission, or validation?** No
- **Does this change affect session state, memory, or transcript integrity?** No
- **Does this change affect provider/model routing or failover behavior?** No - it only affects how the already-classified error is presented to users

## Repro + Verification

**Environment**: Windows 11, Node v24.11.1, pnpm 11.2.2

**Steps to reproduce** (source-level):
1. Trigger a provider failure with message "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6pm (UTC)"
2. Observe the failover layer classifies this as `FailoverError.reason = "rate_limit"`
3. Before fix: `isRateLimitErrorMessage(message)` returns false (pattern not matched)
4. After fix: `isFailoverError(err) && err.reason === "rate_limit"` returns true

**Expected**: Rate-limit error message surfaces in group chats
**Actual (before)**: Silent failure (SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN)
**Actual (after)**: Rate-limit cooldown message surfaces

## Evidence

**Before** (simulated):
```
FailoverError: "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6pm (UTC)"
  reason: "rate_limit"
  
isRateLimitErrorMessage("You've hit your weekly limit...") → false
→ isRateLimit = false
→ buildExternalRunFailureReply → SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN
→ normalizer drops it → no visible reply
```

**After** (simulated):
```
FailoverError: "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6pm (UTC)"
  reason: "rate_limit"
  
isFailoverError(err) && err.reason === "rate_limit" → true
→ isRateLimit = true
→ buildRateLimitCooldownMessage → "API rate limit reached. Please try again later."
→ surfaces in group chat
```

**Test evidence**:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  234 passed (234)
```

## Human Verification

**What was verified**:
- Source-level reproduction of the classification bug
- All existing tests pass (234 tests in agent-runner-execution.test.ts)
- The fix handles both FailoverError and non-FailoverError cases correctly
- No whitespace or formatting errors (git diff --check clean)

**Edge cases checked**:
- Non-FailoverError errors still use message-pattern matching (backward compatible)
- FallbackSummaryError cases still use isPureTransientRateLimitSummary
- Both code paths fixed (~1153 and ~3453)

**What was NOT verified**:
- Live Telegram/group-chat reproduction (no production credentials available)
- Other channel-specific behaviors beyond what tests cover

## Review Conversations

- [x] I have responded to all Codex/ClawSweeper review comments on this PR
- [x] I have addressed or explained why I'm not addressing any bot review comments

## Compatibility / Migration

**Backward compatible**: Yes. The fix only affects errors that are already classified as FailoverError with reason="rate_limit" or "overloaded". Non-FailoverError errors continue to use the existing message-pattern matching.

**Migration needed**: No. This is a pure bug fix with no config or API surface changes.

## Failure Recovery

**How to revert**: `git revert <commit-sha>` - this is a single-commit fix

## Risks and Mitigations

**Risk**: Low. The fix is narrowly scoped to two specific lines and follows the existing pattern for billing error classification.

**Mitigation**: All 234 existing tests pass, confirming no regression in failure handling logic.

target.title: fix(codex): fail closed on unknown projector statuses and warn on protocol drift
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99269.

The Codex event projector had three fail-open or silent-drop paths that turned future Codex protocol drift into wrong results instead of diagnosable errors:

1. `itemStatus()` mapped any unrecognized item status to `"completed"`.
2. The notification dispatch `default:` case silently ignored unknown methods.
3. Thread/turn correlation mismatches were discarded without logging.

A follow-up concern from review: valid **statusless** items (e.g. `webSearch` completions) must remain `"completed"`, while only an **explicit unknown status value** should fail closed. Valid **unscoped/global** Codex notifications (currently `turn/plan/updated`) must also not be logged as active-turn drift, while scoped notifications that lack correlation ids are correctly reported as drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

The harness pins `@openai/codex` 0.142.4 but accepts configured binaries down to the 0.125.0 floor, and the pin is bumped regularly. Status drift produces false success for failed tool calls, while silent drops make upgrade regressions look like nondeterministic model behavior.

`webSearch` and similar items legitimately omit the `status` field, so the missing-status path is preserved as `"completed"`.

## User Impact

Operators and developers will now see explicit warnings when the Codex projector encounters an unknown status value, unknown notification method, or unexpected thread/turn correlation. Unknown item statuses are treated as failures instead of successes, preventing the model from continuing on wrong premises. Statusless `webSearch` completions continue to project as completed, and unscoped/global notifications are not reported as drift.

## Evidence

### Unit-test coverage

Added regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts`:

- **Statusless `webSearch` completion** is projected as `"completed"` and does **not** log an unknown-status warning.
- Unknown item status (`"timedOut"`) is projected as `"failed"` with `isError: true` and emits the expected warning.
- Unknown notification methods emit the expected warning.
- Notifications for a different turn emit the expected warning with expected/actual thread and turn ids.
- Unscoped global notifications (`turn/plan/updated`) do **not** emit an active-turn mismatch warning.
- **Scoped events without thread/turn ids** emit an active-turn mismatch warning.

### Upstream protocol check

Verified upstream Codex item status enum values (`inProgress | completed | failed | declined`) by inspecting the sibling `codex` checkout at `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs`.

### Projector-harness proof transcript

A standalone projector harness drove `CodexAppServerEventProjector` directly through the five drift scenarios (outside the Vitest unit-test suite). The harness script is not committed in order to keep `lint:plugins:no-extension-src-imports` green; the redacted live terminal transcript is preserved here.

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-protocol-drift.mts
[agent/embedded] codex app-server unknown item status treated as failed
[agent/embedded] codex app-server unknown notification method
[agent/embedded] codex app-server notification does not match active turn
=== Codex app-server protocol drift projector-harness proof ===

1. Statusless webSearch completion:
   projected status: completed
   expected: completed

2. commandExecution with explicit unknown status 'timedOut':
   projected status: failed
   projected isError: true
   expected: failed / true

3. Warning log summary:
   - codex app-server unknown item status treated as failed
   - codex app-server unknown notification method
   - codex app-server notification does not match active turn

4. Checks:
   statusless webSearch -> completed: PASS
   unknown status -> failed + warning: PASS
   unknown method -> warning: PASS
   scoped mismatch -> warning: PASS
   unscoped global -> no drift warning: PASS

OVERALL: PASS
```

### Unit-test run

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts --reporter=verbose
...
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > treats statusless webSearch completions as completed
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > treats unknown item statuses as failed
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > does not warn on unscoped global notifications
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > warns on scoped events without thread/turn ids
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > warns on unknown notification methods
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > warns on notifications for a different turn

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  131 passed (131)
```

### Extension boundary checks

- `pnpm lint:plugins:no-extension-src-imports` passes.
- `pnpm lint:extensions:no-relative-outside-package` passes.
- `pnpm lint:extensions:no-plugin-sdk-internal` passes.
- `pnpm lint:extensions:no-src-outside-plugin-sdk` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes.

### Formatting

`pnpm format:check` passes on the changed files.

## Maintainer acceptance requested

This PR intentionally changes the projector behavior so that **explicit unknown item status values** are treated as failures rather than successes. Statusless items (e.g. `webSearch` completions) remain `completed`. Requesting maintainer review and acceptance of this fail-closed compatibility tradeoff before merge.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression policy to media:// references
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: media:// image references, explicit model calls, and CLI infer image describe all bypassed image compression policy, causing oversized photos to fail with provider dimension limit errors
- Solution: Thread model-catalog mediaInput.image limits (maxSidePx, maxPixels, maxBytes) into media-understanding compression policy, covering all three entry points — channel-triggered, runtime API, and CLI --model
- What changed: 6 files (+154/-14)
  - runner.entries.ts: export resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig with provider/model opts; query bundled static catalog for mediaInput.image limits
  - runtime.ts: delete duplicate config-only function; pass provider/model through prepareImageDescriptionInput
  - capability-cli.ts: pass activeModel.provider/model into prepareImageDescriptionInput
- What did NOT change: image tool, HEIC normalization, web-media helpers, config surface

Fixes #101923

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** 4096x4096 images reaching provider without model-aware compression, bypassing catalog dimension caps
- **Real environment tested:** Linux Node 22, worktree with pnpm install + pnpm build
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
# Generate oversized test image
convert -size 4096x4096 xc:red /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png
# Run integrated pipeline with model-aware policy
```
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
BEFORE: /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png PNG 4096x4096
POLICY: {"quality":"balanced","models":[{"preferredSidePx":2048},{"maxSidePx":2576,"preferredSidePx":2576}]}
AFTER: /tmp/test-optimized.png JPEG 2048x2048
VERDICT: 4096x4096 → 2048x2048 ✅
```
- **Observed result after fix:** 4096x4096 PNG compressed to 2048x2048 JPEG. Policy correctly merges agents.defaults (preferredSidePx:2048) with catalog mediaInput.image (maxSidePx:2576, preferredSidePx:2576 from anthropic/claude-sonnet-5). All three code paths now pass provider/model into compression resolution.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider execution (no API keys). Image processing pipeline and policy resolution validated end-to-end; image tool uses the same catalog lookup for live calls.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit tests
- Target test files: image.test.ts (30), runtime.test.ts (21), runner.entries.guards.test.ts (12) — 63 tests all passing
- Scenario locked in: image normalization, runtime file APIs, entry guards, CLI model fallback
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: fix reuses proven helpers (resolveBundledStaticCatalogModel, optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia); tests already cover the full image processing pipeline

## Root Cause

- Root cause: resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig only read agents.defaults (preferredSidePx), producing a policy without hard maxSidePx/maxPixels. optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia preserves originals when no hard constraints exist. The CLI --model path also called preparation before provider/model were known.
- Missing detection: no test verifying media-understanding applies the same model-aware policy as the image tool

## Risk checklist

- **Backward compatibility:** ✅ optional opts added; callers without opts get config-only behavior
- **Config contract:** ✅ uses existing agents.defaults + bundled static catalog
- **Provider contracts:** ✅ respects catalog mediaInput.image limits
- **HEIC conversion:** ✅ preserved
- **Performance:** ✅ process-stable catalog lookup
- **Side effects:** ✅ only media-understanding image paths

target.title: feat(telegram): show quiet-tool progress draft in partial streaming mode
target.body:
Fixes #102587

## What Problem This Solves

With Telegram's default `streaming.mode: "partial"`, a turn doing long tool work streams nothing — partial mode only previews assistant prose, and a tool-grinding turn produces none. Users watch a typing indicator for 20+ minutes and conclude the bot is dead (observed twice in production on 2026-07-09; group members explicitly asked "is it dead?" while the agent was healthy).

## Why This Change Was Made

`streaming.mode: "progress"` already renders a rolling activity draft but is opt-in config with no session command. This change gives `partial` mode a bounded fallback instead of changing defaults: when a turn has tool activity but no visible channel output for 2 minutes, one activity draft appears (same compositor line rendering `progress` mode uses), refreshing on later tool starts no faster than every 30 s. As soon as answer prose streams, the normal partial draft takes over and the fallback is suppressed; room-event turns, `off`/`block`/`progress` modes, and `preview.toolProgress: false` are unaffected. No new config keys — two documented constants.

Scope note: Telegram-only by design; Discord/other edit-capable channels are a follow-up once this shape proves out (#102587 tracks the generic complement to #102468).

## User Impact

A long tool-heavy turn in a default-configured Telegram chat now shows "what it's doing" after two quiet minutes instead of pure silence. Short turns and prose-streaming turns look exactly as before.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` → 176 passed (new: threshold render, prose transition without duplication, pre-threshold visible output suppression, refresh throttle, room-event silence, fast-mode auto-progress regression)
- Full extension sweep `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` → 132 files / 2455 tests passed
- Affected-test grep sweep → 3 shards / 237 tests passed
- tsgo core + extensions lanes green; oxfmt clean; `git diff --check` clean
- Structured autoreview: one finding (fast-mode auto-progress payload dropped in partial mode) accepted, fixed, and regression-covered; final review clean

target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR2/5 in the durable runtime stack. It implements the durable runtime core on top of canonical PR1 #101828, adding persistent runtime state, recovery/orchestration primitives, gateway/operator surfaces, and tests while preserving the PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR2/5
- Canonical upstream gate: PR1 #101828 is 🦐 gold shrimp / threshold-met.
- PR: #102495
- Branch: `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-core-v2-pr101828-ready`
- Current head: `e37c3d5840` (`fix(chat): restore pairing QR display block`)
- Intended base: `origin/pr/101828` at `98ffd6a2fb`

## What Problem This Solves

Agent/session work currently has runtime state and lifecycle edges that are difficult to recover, replay, or reason about across process failures. This PR adds the durable runtime core needed to persist task/run state, recover or fan in work safely, expose gateway controls, and keep embedded-agent session effects typed and observable while preserving canonical PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Scope

- Durable runtime model, SQLite store, recovery/fan-in/orchestration primitives, worker surface, and gateway methods.
- Agent/session runtime effects and context refs needed for durable runs.
- Guardrails/tests for schema lifecycle, task completion policy, gateway protocol, and embedded-agent retry behavior.
- Webchat pairing QR display preservation so sensitive QR setup data is displayed transiently without being persisted into transcript history.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Does not submit PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery-only stack item.

target.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue
target.body:
Fixes #79589

## Problem

Upstream added priority scheduling (foreground/normal/background) via insertion-sort at enqueue time (#82765). Within a static priority tier, older background work can still sit behind later background work indefinitely when the lane stays busy.

## Fix

Implement a **foreground-preserving one-tier aging** policy:

- After `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30s), an entry is promoted by **exactly one priority tier** (`priority + 1`).
- Background (-1) ages to normal (0), still below fresh foreground (1).
- Fresh user/foreground work always runs before aged background.
- Aged background still beats fresh background at the same static priority.

This intentionally does **not** promote aged work to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` or above fresh foreground. The contract is fairness among same-or-lower tiers without starving interactive work.

Files:
- `lanes.ts`: export `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS`
- `command-queue.ts`: `effectivePriority()` (+1 after threshold) and `pickNextIndex()` (effective priority, then oldest enqueue time, then sequence)
- `command-queue.test.ts`: one-tier aging regression tests using `enqueueCommandInLane(CommandLane.Main, ...)`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Command-lane drain selects aged background before fresh background after 30s, while still preferring fresh foreground over aged background (one-tier aging).

**Real environment tested:** macOS, Node from the local OpenClaw checkout, branch `feat/command-queue-priority` at head `41cd18a776`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /tmp/oc-75299
node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
```

**Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched branch:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/process/command-queue.test.ts -t "aged background"
 ✓ command queue > preserves foreground priority over aged background work
 ✓ command queue > promotes aged background above fresh background (one-tier starvation guard)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 30 skipped (32)
```

Source confirmation of the one-tier policy:

```console
$ grep -n "STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS\|return entry.priority" src/process/lanes.ts src/process/command-queue.ts
src/process/lanes.ts:15:export const STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS = 30_000;
src/process/command-queue.ts:282:  if (Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt >= STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS) {
src/process/command-queue.ts:283:    return entry.priority + 1;
src/process/command-queue.ts:285:  return entry.priority;
```

Behavioral contract exercised by the two tests:
1. Aged background then fresh foreground drain order: `["foreground", "background"]`
2. Aged background then fresh background drain order: `["aged-bg", "fresh-bg"]`

**Observed result after fix:** One-tier aging raises background to normal after 30s so it beats later background work, while fresh foreground still wins over aged background. Policy, comments, tests, and this proof describe the same contract.

**What was not tested:** Live gateway under wall-clock multi-session contention with real cron/foreground traffic.

target.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization
target.body:
Fixes #90010
Fixes #79588

## Summary

Improve compaction identifier survival with transcript-wide extraction and quality-guard retry hints. Fixes two security/correctness issues found during review:

**Fix 1 — Sanitize string-encoded JSON arguments before extraction**: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` now parses string-encoded tool arguments as JSON and passes the parsed object through `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before identifier scanning. Previously, string arguments (e.g. OpenAI's JSON-stringified format) were appended raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`.

**Fix 2 — Fail strict compaction when cap recovery cannot fit**: When strict mode detects that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, compaction is now cancelled instead of returning a summary with known identifier loss. This prevents the session from continuing in a state where strict-required identifiers are silently dropped.

## Changed files

- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts` — Parse string args as JSON, sanitize via `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before appending; non-JSON strings still pass through
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` — Cancel compaction (return `{ cancel: true }` with reason) when strict cap recovery overflows instead of silently skipping
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` — Three regression tests: string-encoded JSON credential sanitization, non-JSON passthrough, strict-mode cap overflow cancel

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Two security/correctness issues in compaction identifier survival. (1) `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` appended string-encoded tool arguments raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`. (2) When strict mode detected that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, the summary was returned with known identifier loss instead of cancelling compaction.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5 arm64, Node v22.19.0, pnpm v11.2.2. Built from source on branch `compaction-identifier-survival-validation` at `/tmp/wt-75336`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Create proof script exercising production `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers`, `extractOpaqueIdentifiers`, `extractIdentifiersFromMessages`, `computeLostIdentifiers`, and `capCompactionSummary`:

```typescript
import {
  extractMessageTextForIdentifiers,
  extractOpaqueIdentifiers,
  extractIdentifiersFromMessages,
  computeLostIdentifiers,
} from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.js";
import { testing } from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.js";
const { capCompactionSummary, MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS } = testing;
```

Step 2. Validate Fix 1, string-encoded JSON args with credential `token` field:

```typescript
const msg = {
  role: "assistant",
  content: [{
    type: "functionCall", id: "call_1", name: "configure",
    arguments: '{"token":"deadbeef12345678","endpoint":"https://api.acme.io/v2"}',
  }],
};
const text = extractMessageTextForIdentifiers(msg);
assert(!text.includes("deadbeef12345678"));    // credential redacted
assert(text.includes("https://api.acme.io/v2")); // non-credential survives
```

Step 3. Validate Fix 2, capping loses identifiers and recovery overflows:

```typescript
const transcriptIds = extractIdentifiersFromMessages([
  { role: "user", content: "deploy hash a1b2c3d4e5f6" },
]);
const oversized = "## Decisions\nKeep flow.\n## Exact identifiers\n"
  + "x".repeat(MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS) + "\na1b2c3d4e5f6";
const capped = capCompactionSummary(oversized);
const lost = computeLostIdentifiers(transcriptIds, capped);
assert(lost.length > 0);  // identifier at tail truncated by capping
const recovered = `${capped}\n\n## Exact identifiers (recovered)\n- ${lost[0]}`;
assert(recovered.length > MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS); // recovery overflows
```

Step 4. Run `npx tsx proof-75336.ts` from the patched branch.

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ cd /tmp/wt-75336 && npx tsx proof-75336.ts

[Proof 1] String-encoded JSON args sanitization
  PASS credential token value is redacted from string args
  PASS non-credential endpoint survives sanitization
  PASS hex identifier extractor does not capture redacted credential
  PASS non-JSON string args pass through for extraction

[Proof 2] Identifier loss detection after capping
  PASS transcript identifiers extracted from messages
  PASS hex identifier normalized to uppercase
  PASS capped summary respects size limit
  PASS identifier at tail is lost after capping
  PASS recovery block exceeds cap (triggers cancel in strict mode)

Results: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Observed result after fix:

Fix 1: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` no longer leaks credential-field values from string-encoded JSON arguments. The `token` field value `deadbeef12345678` is redacted by `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before the hex identifier extractor can capture it. Non-credential fields and non-JSON strings pass through normally.

Fix 2: When strict mode detects identifier loss after capping and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000 chars), compaction is cancelled with a diagnostic reason instead of returning a summary with known missing identifiers. The cancel reason is stored via `setCompactionSafeguardCancelReason` for downstream diagnostics.

What was not tested: Live compaction with a real model and conversation history (requires a running OpenClaw session with enough context to trigger compaction).

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1s:

1. Gate post-cap strict identifier recovery/cancel on `qualityGuardEnabled` so `qualityGuard.enabled: false` keeps the opt-out.
2. Redact credential name/value shapes (`token: deadbeef...`) from non-JSON tool argument strings before identifier extraction.

Terminal confirmation:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts -t "redacts credential name|skips post-cap strict|cancels strict compaction when cap"

```

target.title: fix: relay Claude CLI assistant partial messages as streaming deltas
target.body:
Fixes #86050

## Summary

Relay Claude CLI assistant records as streaming deltas so the WebChat UI shows progressive output instead of waiting for the full response.

**Fix 1**: Parse `assistant` records from the Claude CLI JSONL stream and forward their text content as `chat.delta` events.

**Fix 2**: Gate on `stop_reason` using a positive partial signal: only forward records where `stop_reason` is explicitly present and `null` (the documented Claude CLI partial marker). Complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped to avoid duplicating the final message. Records without `stop_reason` at all are ignored as ambiguous (could be complete messages from custom `claude-stream-json` backends).

## Changed files

- `src/agents/cli-output.ts` -- Added `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` with positive `stop_reason: null` guard
- `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` -- Tests covering partial forwarding, complete-message skip, absent-stop_reason rejection, and edge cases

## Verification

All tests use the documented `stop_reason: null` marker for partial messages:
- `stop_reason: null` (explicit) -> text forwarded as streaming delta
- `stop_reason: "end_turn"` -> record skipped (complete message, not a partial)
- `stop_reason` absent -> record skipped (not a confirmed partial; prevents false delivery from custom backends)
- Non-assistant record types -> ignored by the parser
- Malformed content arrays -> returns null without throwing
- Mixed text + tool_use content -> text extracted, tool_use entries ignored

Fixes #86050

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Claude CLI assistant records are not relayed as streaming deltas, so WebChat waits for the full response. The `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function requires a positive partial signal (`stop_reason: null` explicitly present) to skip complete messages and forward only true streaming partials as `chat.delta` events.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5, Node v22.19, OpenClaw built from branch `fix/gateway-stream-relay` at `/tmp/proof-86649`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Build from branch and verify the partial assistant delta parser is active in compiled production code.
Step 2. Feed four Claude CLI JSONL records through the production `createCliJsonlStreamingParser`: two partials (`stop_reason: null`), one complete (`stop_reason: "end_turn"`), and one ambiguous (no `stop_reason` field).

Evidence after fix: terminal output from the patched build:

The partial assistant delta parser and its `stop_reason: null` guard are active in the compiled production bundle:

```console
$ grep -n "parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta\|stop_reason.*null\|partialDelta" dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js
216:function parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta(params) {
220:if (!isRecord$1(message) || !("stop_reason" in message) || message.stop_reason !== null) return null;
394:const partialDelta = parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta({
402:if (partialDelta) {
403:assistantText = partialDelta.text;
404:params.onAssistantDelta(partialDelta);
```

Runtime exercise of the production parser with Claude CLI JSONL event shapes:

```console
$ npx tsx proof-exercise.ts
=== Feeding Claude CLI JSONL records through production parser ===

Input record 1 (partial, stop_reason: null):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"}]

Input record 2 (partial, stop_reason: null, extended text):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer"}],"stop_reason":null},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]

Input record 3 (complete, stop_reason: "end_turn"):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Here is the answer to your question."}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Complete message skipped (no new delta), avoiding duplicate delivery

Input record 4 (no stop_reason field, ambiguous source):
  {"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Some response"}]},"session_id":"sess-abc123"}
  -> Deltas so far: [{"text":"Here is","delta":"Here is"},{"text":"Here is the answer","delta":" the answer"}]
  -> Record without stop_reason skipped (not a confirmed partial)

=== Summary ===
Total records fed: 4
Partial deltas relayed: 2
Delta breakdown:
  [0] delta="Here is" (cumulative: "Here is")
  [1] delta=" the answer" (cumulative: "Here is the answer")

Before fix: Records 1-2 would not emit deltas (assistant type was ignored).
After fix: Records 1-2 relay as streaming deltas. Records 3-4 correctly skipped.
No duplicate final text delivered.
```

Observed result after fix: The compiled production code at `dist/claude-live-session-BYm1bWnI.js:216-220` contains the `parseClaudeCliPartialAssistantDelta` function with the positive partial signal guard (`stop_reason !== null`). At line 394, the main parser calls this function as a fallback when no raw stream delta is available. Runtime exercise confirms: assistant records with `stop_reason: null` relay as incremental streaming deltas (`"Here is"` then `" the answer"`), complete messages with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` are skipped (preventing duplicate delivery), and ambiguous records without `stop_reason` are also skipped (preventing false delivery from custom backends).

What was not tested: Live Claude CLI session with real streaming output over the gateway WebSocket connection. The fix exercises the production parser against the documented Claude CLI JSONL protocol shapes. End-to-end WebChat/TUI display was not verified.

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: route assistant-record partials through commentary classification.

- When classification is active, partial assistant text buffers into `pendingClaudeText` like stream_event text
- Assistant partials that include `tool_use` flush pending narration to `onCommentaryText`
- Regression: pre-tool partial text no longer lands on final assistant deltas

Terminal confirmation:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-output.test.ts -t "partial"
 ✓ streams deltas from Claude assistant partial messages
 ✓ routes assistant partial pre-tool text to commentary when classification is active

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (filtered)
```

Still not tested: live Claude CLI raw stream plus Gateway/WebChat or TUI session (no Claude CLI credentials in this environment).

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** File-source SecretRef in `messages.tts.personas.<id>.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey` is not resolved at runtime, causing `elevenlabs: not configured`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node v22.19.0, OpenClaw built from patched source at `/tmp/wt-89607`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/wt-89607
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm build
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched build:

  The persona-level iteration is active in the production bundle:

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip scheduled heartbeat on idle sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled heartbeats fire every ~30 minutes regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks, silently burning API tokens with no user to receive output. A single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit (#98556).

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults session staleness — `lastInteractionAt` has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception but was never read by the heartbeat runner.
- **Solution**: Gate only ordinary scheduled interval heartbeats (`intent: "scheduled"`) on the resolved session's last interaction time. If `lastInteractionAt` or `sessionStartedAt` is older than 7 days, skip with `reason: "session-idle"`.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (+18 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (+208 lines, 8 test cases)
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, no public API changes. Event/manual/immediate wake intents are not gated. Existing behavior for active sessions is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls firing every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This fix provides a runtime safety guard using a positive-match pattern (`intent: "scheduled"`) to avoid the event-wake delivery regression that blocked the previous attempt (#100852).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Scheduled heartbeats skip on sessions idle longer than 7 days; all other wake intents (event/immediate/manual) are unaffected.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)

$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)

$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Real runtime proof** — direct `runHeartbeatOnce()` call with real session store, real workspace, and real HEARTBEAT.md:

```console
$ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts
=== Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

    status: skipped, reason: empty-heartbeat-file
  ✅ Active session (1 min idle) + scheduled
    status: skipped, reason: session-idle
  ✅ Idle session (8 days) + scheduled → skip
    status: skipped, reason: empty-heartbeat-file
  ✅ Idle session (8 days) + event → NOT skipped

=== Results: 3 passed, 0 failed ===
```

| Test | Scenario | Intent | lastInteractionAt | Idle gate fired? |
|------|----------|--------|-------------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Active session | `scheduled` | 1 min ago | No (different skip: empty-heartbeat-file) |
| 2 | Idle 8 days | `scheduled` | 8 days ago | ✅ Yes → `session-idle` |
| 3 | Idle 8 days | `event` | 8 days ago | ✅ No → event not gated |

**Matrix: idle gate behavior by wake intent**

| Intent | Session state | lastInteractionAt | Result |
|--------|--------------|-------------------|--------|
| `scheduled` | Active (1 min idle) | now - 1m | `ran` (no gate) |
| `scheduled` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `skipped / session-idle` |
| `scheduled` | No entry | undefined | `ran` (no gate) |
| `scheduled` | Exactly at boundary | now - 7d | `ran` (> threshold, not >=) |
| `event` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |
| `immediate` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |
| `manual` | Idle (>7 days) | now - 8d | `ran` (not gated) |

**Fallback chain**:

| Available fields | Behavior |
|-----------------|----------|
| `lastInteractionAt` exists + >7d | Skip |
| `lastInteractionAt` missing, `sessionStartedAt` exists + >7d | Skip (fallback) |
| Neither `lastInteractionAt` nor `sessionStartedAt` | Allow (cannot determine staleness) |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Scheduled heartbeats on sessions idle >7 days: skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. Event/manual/immediate heartbeats on idle sessions: unaffected.
  3. Sessions with recent interaction: unaffected (no behavioral change).
  4. Sessions with no entry or insufficient timestamps: unaffected.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts`) performs 13 skip checks but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

## Regression Test Plan

8 new unit tests cover the idle gate (active session, stale session, all 4 wake intents, fallback to sessionStartedAt, no-entry, boundary). 43 existing heartbeat tests confirm zero regression.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see scheduled heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: Active session, idle session (8 days), all 4 wake intents, no session entry, exactly at 7-day boundary.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined (falls back to `sessionStartedAt`), both undefined, no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for idle sessions; heartbeat behavior for active sessions is completely unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Positive-match on `intent === "scheduled"` avoids the deny-list regression that blocked #100852. The injection point in `runHeartbeatOnce()` (after all other skip conditions, before preflight) is the right boundary because the session entry is already resolved and all four wake intents are known.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because it requires a configured `SessionResetPolicy` which may not be present.
  2. Using `session.resetPolicy.idleMinutes` if configured — over-engineered for a safety guard.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout. That feature requires a product decision and is tracked separately. This PR provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard (7-day threshold) that prevents runaway cost while #14051 is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate low-frequency heartbeat tasks (e.g., a weekly report).
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold uses strict greater-than (`>`, not `>=`), so a weekly heartbeat that fires on day 7 still runs. Only sessions idle longer than 7 days are affected.
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days.
**Scope limitation**: Auth error backoff (repeated `authentication_error` after spend cap) is not addressed — it is a separate defense-in-depth concern tracked in #98556.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

---

Related to #98556
