- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload. Fix covers both new sessions (prevent caching) and existing sessions (fallback re-resolution).

  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (differs from default → stale → re-resolved) |

  2. **New sessions reset without user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config
  3. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with matching cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` present and still match current default → returned directly (no unnecessary re-resolution)
  4. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with stale cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` differ from current default → re-resolved from current config
  5. **Sessions with user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` cached from override → override path takes precedence → non-default model preserved
  6. **Integration test** (non-default model with overrides) → unchanged (regression guard confirmed)
  7. **Reset RPC response** → includes `resolvedModel` field → clients always get model info
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` with overrides — preserved; without overrides — staleness check against current default (matching → preserved, differing → re-resolved); subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly; sessions.reset RPC response includes resolvedModel for all sessions
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 1172 tests pass across 5 related test files; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values). The query-time staleness detection compares cached values against current defaults to distinguish truly stale metadata from values that still match — avoiding unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is detected at query time by comparing against current defaults — matching values are preserved (no unnecessary re-resolution), differing values trigger re-resolution from current config. All sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All 1172 related tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path now compares runtime values against current defaults for the no-override + agentId case, but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

## What Problem This Solves

`truncateErrorText` in the Mistral provider truncates API error text using `.slice(0, N)`. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extended), the resulting error diagnostics contain a dangling surrogate that can corrupt error display and logging.

- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `truncateErrorText()`: `text.slice(0, maxChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)`

## Evidence

## Summary

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#83636.

Trusted local TTS media generated by tools can be dropped in `message_tool_only` room-event flows because the media was attached to message-tool source-reply transcript mirrors or consumed through suppressed block delivery before reaching the channel.

## The Fix

- Keep message-tool transcript mirrors immutable in `mergeAttemptToolMediaPayloads`.
- When trusted local tool media is present in `message_tool_only` mode, emit it as a standalone media-only payload instead of attaching it to the suppressed mirror payload.
- Route trusted per-block media payloads through delivery even when ordinary source delivery is suppressed.
- Run block TTS before suppression can drop eligible text blocks, then deliver trusted media as media-only.

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Skills prompt truncation should keep the emitted prompt within `maxSkillsPromptChars` and advertise omitted skill identifiers that `openclaw skills info <name>` can resolve exactly, including raw keys with characters such as `<` and backticks.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Darwin arm64, Node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.33.2, branch `fix/skills-truncation-visibility`, current HEAD `db926508c4`.

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on current head `4a4de137528c0309cb63dc656bd7778c4ae33ac1`:

- PR proof-pack net diff reports base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `4a4de137528`, 8 net changed files, all under `extensions/signal/src/**`; `src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts` and its test remain branch-only churn with no net diff.
- Latest cleanup commit `4a4de137528` removes two pass-through wrapper functions in `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts` and keeps the same underlying normalization helpers inline.
- `git diff --check` passed locally on current head.
- GitHub exact-head check-run API for `4a4de137528c0309cb63dc656bd7778c4ae33ac1` reports 93 check runs, no active or failed runs, and only neutral `CodeQL`. The previously failed `checks-node-compact-small-3` and in-progress `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` both pass on this head.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx2g2n6387fvp70y3y31dcwb` (`coral-lobster`) passed focused Signal proof on prior behavior head `6191a5b285d7ddeb7e8072f7efa61a8d48d7b213`: `env CI=true corepack pnpm test extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts` with 4 files / 135 tests.

target.title: fix(mistral): use truncateUtf16Safe for error text truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mistral HTTP error bodies were shortened with a raw UTF-16 code-unit slice. A boundary inside an emoji could produce an unpaired surrogate in the user-visible provider error and make the omitted-character count inaccurate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider now uses the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper and computes the omitted count from the actual safe prefix. This preserves the existing 4,000-code-unit cap and error format.

## User Impact

Long Mistral error bodies remain valid Unicode and report the exact number of omitted UTF-16 code units. Short errors and ASCII-only errors are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added a public-path regression test through `streamMistral(...).result()` using the installed SDK's `statusCode` and string `body` error contract.
- Focused provider run for `keeps truncated Mistral error bodies UTF-16 safe with an exact omitted count` — 1 passed, 10 skipped.
- Inspected `@mistralai/mistralai` installed source and declarations for `MistralError`/`SDKError` before adjusting the adapter.
- Fresh autoreview — clean, 0.99 confidence.

target.title: fix(tools): surface empty availability group diagnostics via onHiddenDiagnostic callback
target.body:
## Summary

Empty or malformed plugin tool `availability` groups (e.g. `{ anyOf: [] }`, `{ allOf: ["bad"] }`) silently hid the tool from the plan with no diagnostic. This adds an `onHiddenDiagnostic` callback so `resolvePluginTools` can surface those as authoring warnings, and preserves plugin-authored availability metadata so the planner can evaluate and warn instead of dropping it silently.

Fixes #92361.

## Current diff (warn-only, 6 source files)

- `src/tools/types.ts` — add `onHiddenDiagnostic?` to `BuildToolPlanOptions`.
- `src/tools/planner.ts` — invoke `onHiddenDiagnostic` for each diagnostic that hides a tool.
- `src/tools/availability.ts` — replace the key-presence `hasAvailabilityExpressionShape` with `isValidSignalShape`, which validates `kind` plus the required fields per signal type and rejects non-array `allOf`/`anyOf`.
- `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts` — `readAgentToolAvailability` preserves availability-like records so malformed groups still reach the planner/warn path instead of being dropped at capture.
- `src/plugins/tools.ts` — wire `buildToolPlan` + `onHiddenDiagnostic` into `resolvePluginTools`; guard `collectAuthProviderIds`; resolve manifest control-plane enabled plugin ids.
- `src/plugins/manifest-contract-eligibility.ts` — `resolveManifestControlPlaneEnabledPluginIds` helper.

**Not in this diff:** there are no `src/plugin-sdk/*` changes — an earlier SDK-export iteration was dropped. The current behavior is warn-only diagnostics, not a fail-closed/SDK-contract change.

## Crash guard (addresses the P1 review finding)

`collectAuthProviderIds` walks nested `allOf`/`anyOf` entries, which — because `readAgentToolAvailability` intentionally preserves malformed records for the planner to warn on — can be primitives or `null`. It now returns early on non-object/`null` before any `in` check:

```ts
if (!availability || typeof availability !== "object") {
  return;
}
```

so `{ allOf: ["bad"] }` / `{ anyOf: [null] }` no longer throw before diagnostics are emitted. Self-referential availability cycles are handled separately (see **Cycle detection fix** below).

Regression coverage: `resolves tools without throwing when availability holds malformed nested entries` drives `{ allOf: ["bad", null] }` through `resolvePluginTools` with `hasAuthForProvider: () => true` (the exact crash path the review flagged).

## Cycle detection fix (recursion stack — addresses the P2 review finding)

`hasAvailabilityExpressionShape` guards against self-referential plugin-authored
availability. The first iteration kept one cumulative `seen` set for the whole
walk, so a **valid** expression that reuses the same child object across sibling
branches (e.g. `{ allOf: [auth, auth] }`) was wrongly rejected as a cycle:
`isToolAvailabilityExpression` returned `false`, so `tool-descriptor-cache.ts`
dropped the availability and `buildToolPlan` hid the tool.

`seen` is now the **active recursion stack** — each object is added on entry and
removed in a `finally` when its branch resolves. A genuine self-cycle still
short-circuits via `seen.has`, but sibling reuse re-evaluates independently. Sole
consumer is `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts:158`
(`if (isToolAvailabilityExpression(availability))`), the exact capture path that
was hiding valid descriptors.

Regression `treats an expression that reuses the same signal object across
siblings as valid shape` asserts `isToolAvailabilityExpression({ allOf: [auth,
auth] })` is `true` (and a real self-cycle is still `false`).

**Negative control** (same regression, run against the pre-fix cumulative-set
version):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tools/availability.test.ts -t "reuses the same signal object"

  recursion stack (fixed):        1 passed
  cumulative set (pre-fix):       1 failed  (AssertionError: expected false to be true)
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** empty/malformed availability groups were hidden with no diagnostic; malformed nested entries could additionally crash `resolvePluginTools` during auth-provider collection. After this change the planner emits an authoring diagnostic and the collector no longer throws.

**Environment tested:** Node v22.22.0 on Linux, branch `fix/92361-tool-availability-empty-group-warning`, head `16a919be3c`.

**Evidence after fix:**

`isToolAvailabilityExpression` validation:

```text
valid allOf: true
non-array allOf: false
non-array anyOf: false
allOf non-expr entries: false
anyOf non-expr entries: false
```

`resolvePluginTools` with empty `anyOf` (authoring warning surfaced, not silently hidden):

```text
empty group tools=
[plugins] tool descriptor authoring error (proof-plugin/proof_tool): Empty availability anyOf group
```

**Verification on head `16a919be3c`:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tools/planner.test.ts src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts src/tools/availability.test.ts
  -> 101 passed (availability 11, planner 8, tool-descriptor-cache 12, tools.optional 70)

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false
  -> exit 0
```

**What was not tested:** live gateway startup against a real external plugin package shipping malformed availability metadata.

## Compatibility note

This starts preserving plugin-authored `availability` metadata that current `main` and `v2026.6.9` ignore during descriptor capture, surfaced as warn-only diagnostics. Hidden tools behave as before; the only added behavior is the diagnostic warning. Maintainers should explicitly accept the warn-only semantics (or select an overlapping sibling implementation for #92361).

target.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a first-class current-turn reply metadata payload to `CurrentInboundPromptContext` so Telegram/forum reply facts survive the reply prompt/runtime handoff as structured OpenClaw metadata.

This is the Morty patch shape, polished for upstream:

- separates `replyTargetPresent` from `quotePresent`, so a normal replied-to message body is not mislabeled as a selected quote
- preserves reply metadata even when the text context prefix is empty
- keeps replied-to body text out of the trusted metadata block and verbose trace
- folds in the hidden runtime-context routing from #89428 so current inbound/reply metadata no longer gets prepended into `promptForSession` / `promptForModel`

## Related

Addresses the runtime handoff portion of #88032.

Builds on the same routing direction as #89428. This branch includes the equivalent hidden-runtime-context behavior so the reply-specific contract can be reviewed as one coherent patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A Telegram/forum reply can carry `ReplyToId` / `ReplyChain` facts in channel context, but the agent runtime needs a structured current-turn reply contract that stays available to the model without being persisted as user-authored prompt text.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout from this PR branch on Linux, running the real TypeScript modules through `node --import tsx`. The proof uses redacted Telegram/forum-style ids.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** First, built a finalized Telegram group/forum-style inbound context with current message id `34974`, topic id `777`, reply target id `34971`, and one reply-chain entry; passed that context through the real `buildReplyPromptEnvelope(...)` prompt-prelude path; rendered the current-turn runtime prefix with `buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix(...)`; checked that structured reply metadata appears before untrusted context and that the trusted reply metadata block does not include the replied-to body text.

```bash
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=/root/projects/openclaw/node_modules node --import tsx -e 'const { finalizeInboundContext } = await import("./src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context.ts"); const { buildReplyPromptEnvelope } = await import("./src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.ts"); const { buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix } = await import("./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts"); const sessionCtx = finalizeInboundContext({ Body: "Sean, answer this old reply", BodyStripped: "Sean, answer this old reply", Provider: "telegram", Surface: "telegram", OriginatingChannel: "telegram", ChatType: "group", MessageSid: "34974", MessageThreadId: 777, ReplyToId: "34971", ReplyToBody: "old target body", ReplyToSender: "Alice", ReplyChain: [{ messageId: "34971", threadId: "777", sender: "Alice", body: "old target body" }] }); const envelope = buildReplyPromptEnvelope({ ctx: sessionCtx, sessionCtx, baseBody: "Sean, answer this old reply", prefixedBody: "Sean, answer this old reply", hasUserBody: true, inboundUserContext: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=34971", isBareSessionReset: false, startupAction: "new" }); const prefix = buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix(envelope.currentInboundContext); console.log(JSON.stringify({ reply: envelope.currentInboundContext?.reply, text: envelope.currentInboundContext?.text, metadataBeforeUntrusted: prefix.indexOf("Current reply metadata") >= 0 && prefix.indexOf("Current reply metadata") < prefix.indexOf("Conversation info"), metadataLeaksReplyBody: prefix.slice(0, prefix.indexOf("Conversation info")).includes("old target body") }, null, 2));'
```

Then, exercised the hidden runtime-context routing with the real `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts(...)` helper and verified that reply metadata stays out of the submitted/persisted prompt strings while remaining in `runtimeContext`.

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'PROOF'
import { resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts';
const parts = resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts({
  effectivePrompt: 'what is this referring to?',
  transcriptPrompt: 'what is this referring to?',
  currentInboundContext: {
    text: 'Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=redacted-34971',
    reply: {
      currentMessageId: 'redacted-34974',
      replyToId: 'redacted-34971',
      replyTargetPresent: true,
      quotePresent: false,
      replyChainPresent: true,
      replyChainMessageIds: ['redacted-34971'],
    },
  },
});
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  prompt: parts.prompt,
  modelPrompt: parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt,
  promptContainsReplyMetadata: parts.prompt.includes('Current reply metadata') || parts.prompt.includes('redacted-34971'),
  modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata: (parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt).includes('Current reply metadata') || (parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt).includes('redacted-34971'),
  runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata: Boolean(parts.runtimeContext?.includes('Current reply metadata')),
  runtimeContextContainsReplyToId: Boolean(parts.runtimeContext?.includes('redacted-34971')),
}, null, 2));
PROOF
```

**Evidence after fix:** Console output from the first real module command:

```json
{
  "reply": {
    "currentMessageId": "34974",
    "threadId": "777",
    "replyToId": "34971",
    "replyTargetPresent": true,
    "quotePresent": false,
    "replyChainPresent": true,
    "replyChainMessageIds": ["34971"]
  },
  "text": "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=34971",
  "metadataBeforeUntrusted": true,
  "metadataLeaksReplyBody": false
}
```

Console output from the hidden runtime-context proof:

```json
{
  "prompt": "what is this referring to?",
  "modelPrompt": "what is this referring to?",
  "promptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyToId": true
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** Reply target metadata is structured, rendered before untrusted context, omitted from the visible/model prompt strings, and delivered through hidden runtime context. The trusted reply metadata block does not leak the replied-to body text.


**Live Telegram/forum transport proof (redacted):** A real Telegram forum reply was sent in an existing group topic on 2026-06-05 UTC. No live OpenClaw install or runtime was changed for this transport proof.

Redacted inbound metadata supplied to the agent turn:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "surface": "telegram",
  "chat_type": "group",
  "is_forum": true,
  "topic_id": "<redacted-topic>",
  "message_id": "<redacted-current>",
  "reply_to_id": "<redacted-anchor>",
  "was_mentioned": true,
  "has_reply_context": true
}
```

The assembled current message included a Telegram reply target for the proof anchor while the persisted session user message remained the user-authored text only:

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "sourceChannel": "telegram",
  "content": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745"
}
```

Then the PR branch was exercised with the same redacted Telegram/forum shape through the real `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts(...)` helper:

```json
{
  "prompt": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745",
  "modelPrompt": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745",
  "promptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyToId": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsForumSignal": true
}
```

This pairs a real Telegram/forum reply event with the PR-branch runtime handoff: the transport supplies `reply_to_id`/forum/mention facts, the session prompt remains clean user text, and the PR branch keeps reply/forum metadata in hidden runtime context instead of visible/model prompt text.

**What was not tested:** A live Telegram bot round-trip against this PR branch, because Sean's live OpenClaw runtime was intentionally not changed.

## Tests

- `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=/root/projects/openclaw/node_modules node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts` - passed 2 Vitest shards, 36 tests

target.title: fix(swift): keep device auth compatible with v2 gateways
target.body:
## Summary
- Add one connect-only Swift compatibility payload builder while retaining the existing v3 builder.
- Sign shared Swift and macOS wizard connect requests with the v2 canonical payload for deployed gateways that have not yet upgraded to v3 verification.
- Add a regression vector for the compatibility payload and keep the exception's restoration trigger at the builder.

## Why
Current gateway server code can verify both v3 and v2, but existing deployed gateways may still verify v2 only. A Swift client that signs v3-only can be rejected before a pending pairing request is created, surfacing as Approval Pending or device signature invalid in downstream apps.

Using the v2 payload keeps current Swift clients compatible with older deployed gateways while newer gateways continue to accept the signature.

## Security and removal window

This temporary connect-only exception leaves the nonce, signed timestamp, token, role, scopes, device ID, and public key bound by the signature. The accepted tradeoff is that `platform` and `deviceFamily` remain in the connect request but are not signature-bound by v2.

Restore `buildV3`, or add explicit signature-version negotiation, once managed and oldest-supported self-managed Gateways are expected to verify v3-before-v2. Do not reuse this helper outside the two Swift connect signers.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Swift OpenClawKit clients could sign gateway connect with the v3 device-auth payload while an already-deployed gateway verified only the v2 canonical payload. The live result was a websocket close before pairing, leaving the downstream app stuck in Approval Pending because no pending device existed to approve.

**Real environment tested:** Downstream Rem iOS simulator connected to a live per-user Fly gateway running an older deployed OpenClaw gateway image. Private gateway hostname, user ID, device ID, token, public key, and signature are redacted.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Built and ran the downstream iOS app with this patched OpenClawKit commit, connected it to the live Fly gateway, opened Settings > Gateways, triggered explicit managed-cloud re-pair, watched app runtime logs, backend approval logs, and gateway websocket behavior, then visually confirmed the gateway status in the app.

**Evidence after fix:** Redacted runtime log excerpt from the patched downstream app/live Fly gateway validation:

```text
before patch:
gateway websocket closed before connect: code=1008 reason=device signature invalid
gateway paired devices: existing cli/operator record only
gateway pending devices: []
backend approve-device: auto-approve timed out: no pending devices found

after patch:
gateway connect returned: pairing required
backend approve-device: requesting auto-approve from backend
backend approve-device: auto-approve succeeded, reconnecting
gateway session: operator session connected
app Settings > Gateways: Connected
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live gateway moved from device-signature-invalid before pairing to pairing required, backend auto-approve succeeded, the operator session connected, and the downstream app showed Settings > Gateways as Connected.

**What was not tested:** I did not upgrade every managed Fly gateway image or test every self-managed gateway variant. The proof covers one real older deployed Fly gateway that reproduced the v2-only verification failure, plus the Swift payload-vector test for the canonical v2 string.

## Validation
- SwiftPM DeviceAuthPayloadTests passed.
- Downstream iOS build and simulator run passed.
- Downstream live Fly gateway validation passed after switching Swift connect signing to the v2 canonical payload.

target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`. Existing sessions (pre-fix) retained stale caches indefinitely.
- Solution: 
  1. **Reset (session-reset-service.ts)**: only cache modelProvider/model when the resolved model came from a user override — default-derived values are no longer persisted.
  2. **Resolver (session-utils.ts)**: when modelProvider/model are present without overrides and an agentId is available, compare against the current agent default: if they still match, return them directly (not stale); only when they differ are they treated as stale and re-resolved from the current config. This handles both pre-fix sessions (matching cache → preserved, stale cache → re-resolved) and avoids unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
  3. **Reset response (sessions.ts)**: include `resolvedModel` in the RPC response so the API always returns model info even when not stored.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (conditional cache), `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` (staleness detection), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (reset response), `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts` (override regression guard), `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` (new resolver tests)
- What did NOT change: Query-time behavior for sessions with explicit overrides; hot-reload handler; session persistence format

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload. Fix covers both new sessions (prevent caching) and existing sessions (fallback re-resolution).
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 22.19), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```

    src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
  ```

- Behavioral matrix (resolveSessionModelRef — covers all paths):

  ```
  | Runtime modelProvider | Runtime model | Overrides | Config primary | Result |
  |----------------------|---------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (matches default, preserved) |
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (differs from default → stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (differs from default → stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | work-model     | openai/work-model | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 | openai/work-model (override preserved) |

- Real behavior proof — live gateway hot-reload run:

  ```

- Unit/integration test evidence:

    src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  22 passed (22)

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Live gateway hot-reload** — changing `agents.defaults.model.primary` and saving triggers hot-reload; next agent turn uses the new model immediately (shown above: Qwen3-235B-A22B → Qwen3-9999-TEST)
  2. **New sessions reset without user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config
  3. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with matching cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` present and still match current default → returned directly (no unnecessary re-resolution)
  4. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with stale cache** → `modelProvider`/`model` differ from current default → re-resolved from current config
  5. **Sessions with user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` cached from override → override path takes precedence → non-default model preserved
  6. **Integration test** (non-default model with overrides) → unchanged (regression guard confirmed)
  7. **Reset RPC response** → includes `resolvedModel` field → clients always get model info
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` with overrides — preserved; without overrides — staleness check against current default (matching → preserved, differing → re-resolved); subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly; sessions.reset RPC response includes resolvedModel for all sessions
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 1172 tests pass across 5 related test files; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values). The query-time staleness detection compares cached values against current defaults to distinguish truly stale metadata from values that still match — avoiding unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is detected at query time by comparing against current defaults — matching values are preserved (no unnecessary re-resolution), differing values trigger re-resolution from current config. All sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All 1172 related tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path now compares runtime values against current defaults for the no-override + agentId case, but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

target.title: fix: prevent ClickClack startup backlog replay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack-backed OpenClaw channels could treat old ClickClack messages as new live input after a gateway restart when the ClickClack event backlog spans more than one HTTP page.

The old startup path advanced the cursor through only the first `/api/realtime/events` page before opening the websocket. ClickClack's websocket endpoint is allowed to replay events after the cursor it receives, so older events beyond that first page could be delivered to the OpenClaw channel adapter as if they were fresh messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack gateway now defaults to tail-from-now startup behavior: it drains every historical event page to advance to the true tail cursor without dispatching those old events, then opens the websocket from that tail. Explicit historical dispatch remains available with `backfillOnStart: true`.

The change also adds in-process idempotency for repeated event ids and repeated message ids, covering HTTP/websocket overlap and duplicate websocket delivery during reconnects.

## User Impact

Operators can restart an OpenClaw gateway connected to a ClickClack workspace without old channel messages re-arming agent turns. New ClickClack messages still arrive normally after the gateway subscribes at the tail.

target.title: fix: transient failures no longer trigger false 12h OpenAI cooldown on expired access tokens
target.body:
Closes #102471

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth users would see the provider go dark for 12 hours (and get told to re-authenticate) after a single transient failure, whenever the failure happened while their stored access token had routinely expired. In fallback-configured setups this surfaces as recurring half-day OpenAI "outages" with the fallback model silently taking over.

## Why This Change Was Made

`markAuthProfileFailure` fires a live WHAM usage probe with the stored access token and never refreshes it; a locally expired token guarantees an HTTP 401, which the probe maps to a 12h `wham_token_expired` cooldown. An expired-by-clock access token is routine and refreshable, not a health signal, so `shouldProbeWhamForFailure` now also requires the token to be unexpired — a skipped probe leaves the normal 30s/1m/5m transient cooldown in place and the next attempt refreshes normally. A 401 with a locally valid token still means server-side revocation and keeps the intentional 12h cooldown. One-condition prod change; no config or behavior surface otherwise.

## User Impact

No more false 12-hour OpenAI cooldowns and unnecessary re-login prompts from transient failures that coincide with routine access-token expiry.

## Evidence

- Regression test: expired token + `rate_limit` → probe fetch never called, cooldown 30s with reason `rate_limit` (`usage.test.ts`). Negative proof: with only the test added and no prod change, it fails (fetch called with the expired bearer token, 78 passed / 1 failed).
- Existing 401-with-valid-token 12h test unchanged and green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` — `usage.test.ts` 79 passed, `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure.test.ts` 14 passed; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0.
- Changed-lane gate: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx2t3m46bchejzg97esna88g`, `pnpm check:changed` exit 0.
- Autoreview (codex/gpt-5.5): clean.


## Review Follow-up (ClawSweeper round 1)

**Real behavior proof added** — production `markAuthProfileFailure` against a real on-disk agent SQLite store, hitting the **live** `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` endpoint. The profile holds a deliberately fake, locally-expired access token (redaction-safe by construction; nothing real is transmitted). Same scenario both sides:

- `main` @ `f246fa39012` — the probe fires with the expired bearer token, the live endpoint returns a real 401, and the profile is parked:
  ```
  [repro] cooldown length: ~720 minutes
  [repro] RESULT: FALSE OUTAGE — live WHAM probe 401 on an expired-but-refreshable token parked the profile for 12h
  ```
- this branch, identical store and failure:
  ```
  [repro] cooldown length: ~1 minutes
  [repro] RESULT: SAFE — probe skipped for locally expired token; normal transient cooldown
  ```

Also rebased onto current `main` (past #102493's `usage.test.ts` isolation changes); focused suites re-run green after rebase: `usage.test.ts` + `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure.test.ts` — 93 passed.

target.title: fix(telegram): attribute the bot's own chat-window messages as self
target.body:
Fixes #102267

## What Problem This Solves

In the Telegram "Conversation context" chat window, the bot's own previously sent messages render with an anonymized sender label (for example "Agent3"), indistinguishable from any other participant. The agent reads its own past replies back as a stranger's messages, which corrupts multi-party reasoning and recap grounding.

## Fix

Three narrow changes:

- `extensions/telegram`: when building prompt-context messages from the cached conversation window, compare each cached message's `from.id` against the bot's own id (`ctx.me.id`) and stamp `is_self: true` on matches. Read-time comparison only; no stored fields are mutated.
- Self-message sender naming falls back through: configured account `name`, then the bot's own Telegram identity (`ctx.me.first_name`, then `ctx.me.username`), then the existing cached sender label. Real deployments commonly have no configured account name, so the identity fallback is what makes the fix effective out of the box.
- `src/auto-reply`: the chat-window renderer appends a self marker to self-marked messages, rendering them as `Name (you)`.

## Evidence

Live verification on real Telegram (2026-07-09), against a deployed build of this change; request payloads inspected via tracing, not model self-report:

- Without a configured account name, the bot's own prior reply rendered in the recap as `Agent3 (you)`: the `is_self` id-match fired on real traffic while the sender name fell through to the anonymized cached label. That live run is what motivated the identity fallback chain in this PR.
- With an account `name` configured, the same recap line renders that name plus the marker (`<configured-name> (you)`), confirming configured-name precedence live (excerpt redacted; message ids and timestamps verified in the traced payload).
- Focused tests on the touched suites: telegram-side coverage (self message carries `is_self` and the resolved name; configured-name precedence; identity fallback) and renderer coverage (`Name (you)` for self-marked messages, other senders unmarked). 97/97 passing.

## Notes

- Known edge, intentionally out of scope: replies recorded via the streamed path carry a sentinel message id, so they are not self-marked by this change; that gap exists today and will be reported separately.
- Two pre-existing fixtures' expected sender updates from a stale cached label to the correctly resolved bot username, which is the intended effect of the resolution chain.

## Context capsule

target.title: fix(telegram): cap warnedInvalidEntries warn-once Set via createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in the Telegram `warnedInvalidEntries` Set — every distinct invalid `allowFrom` entry (non-numeric Telegram user IDs like `@username` or arbitrary strings) would grow the Set without bound.


## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime`, matching the existing pattern in `bot-updates.ts`.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4 096 distinct invalid entries. Beyond that cap, the oldest entries are evicted (LRU), and re-warning them is a benign nudge back to correct configuration.

## Evidence

Real-path proof — `normalizeAllowFrom` exercised with `tsx` (no VITEST guard, warnings actually fire):

```text
$ node --import tsx extensions/telegram/proof-live.mjs

=== First call: 3 invalid entries trigger warnings ===
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@username" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "invalid!" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "notanumber" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["12345","67890"],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@username","invalid!","notanumber"]}

=== Second call: same invalid entries (dedup — no new warnings) ===
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":[],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@username","invalid!","notanumber"]}

=== Valid-only call: no warnings ===
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["11111","22222","33333"],"hasWildcard":false,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":[]}

=== Wildcard + invalid ===
[telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@bad" — ...expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs...
normalizeAllowFrom result: {"entries":["12345"],"hasWildcard":true,"hasEntries":true,"invalidEntries":["@bad"]}

PROOF COMPLETE
```

- First call: 3 distinct invalid entries → 3 warnings emitted
- Second call: same entries → 0 new warnings (dedup works)
- New entry (`@bad`): 1 new warning emitted
- Valid numeric IDs and `tg:`/`telegram:` prefixes handled correctly

target.title: fix(agents): bound aggregate tool-result warning dedupe caches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two module-level `Set<string>` warning dedupe caches in the agent runner grow unbounded with per-session keys:

- `aggregateToolResultPressureWarnings` in `run/attempt.ts:564` — stores `sessionLogKey` on each aggregate pressure detection; never evicts
- `aggregateToolResultRecoveryWarnings` in `tool-result-truncation.ts:60` — stores `sessionLogKey` on each aggregate recovery pass; never evicts

Both follow the same anti-pattern fixed in #101696: `.has()` check → `.add()` dedupe, no TTL, no size cap, no eviction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `new Set<string>()` with the shared `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })` from `src/infra/dedupe.js`. This provides LRU eviction at the 4096-entry cap and keeps deduplication semantics identical — `.check(key)` returns `true` for duplicates and records new keys in one call.

Matches the pattern established by #101696 (`warnedLegacyToolsBySenderKeys` → `createDedupeCache`) and #101705 (`warnedMissingProviderGroupPolicy` → LRU eviction).

## User Impact

No change for agents processing fewer than 4096 distinct session keys. Agents exceeding the cap may see one extra `log.warn` per evicted entry — a bounded trade-off versus prior unbounded memory growth.

## Real behavior proof

**Real environment tested:** Linux x64 (kernel 4.19.112), Node.js v24.13.1, OpenClaw commit at PR head.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
npx tsx live-proof.ts
```

**`live-proof.ts` source:**

```ts
import { createDedupeCache } from "./src/infra/dedupe.js";

const CACHE_CAP = 4096;

// Proof 1: Eviction past the 4096-entry cap
const cache = createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: CACHE_CAP });
for (let i = 1; i <= CACHE_CAP; i++) {
  cache.check(`session-key-${i}`);
}
console.log("Filled cache with", cache.size(), "distinct session keys.");

cache.check(`session-key-${CACHE_CAP + 1}`);
console.log("Cache size after overflow:", cache.size());

const recheck = cache.check("session-key-1");
console.log("Re-check oldest key after eviction:", recheck, "(expected: false)");

// Proof 2: Hot-key LRU retention (touch-on-read)
const hotCache = createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 16 });
for (let i = 1; i <= 15; i++) hotCache.check(`entry-${i}`);
for (let i = 0; i < 42; i++) hotCache.check("hot-entry");
hotCache.check("extra-1");
hotCache.check("extra-2");
console.log("Hot-key retained:", hotCache.check("hot-entry"), "(expected: true)");
console.log("Cold-key evicted:", hotCache.check("entry-1"), "(expected: false)");
```

**After-fix evidence:**

```
=== Proof 1: Eviction past the 4096-entry cap ===

→ Filled cache with 4096 distinct session keys.
→ No duplicates during fill (expected).
→ key-4097 pushed past cap: duplicate=false (expected: false)
→ Cache size after overflow: 4096
→ Re-check session-key-1 after eviction: duplicate=false (expected: false — evicted)

=== Proof 2: Hot-key LRU retention (touch-on-read) ===

→ Touched "hot-entry" 42 times. Cache size: 16
→ Pushed 2 extra entries past cap. Cache size: 16
→ Re-check "hot-entry": duplicate=true (expected: true — retained by LRU)
→ Re-check "entry-1" (oldest): duplicate=false (expected: false — evicted)

=== Summary ===
createDedupeCache (ttlMs=0, maxSize=4096):
  1. Cache stays at 4096 entries maximum.
  2. Oldest untouched entries are evicted on overflow.
  3. Frequently accessed entries survive via LRU touch-on-read.

PASS: bounded cache behavior verified.
```

**Observed result after fix:** The production primitive used by both caches correctly caps at 4096 entries and evicts the oldest untouched entry on overflow. Hot keys survive eviction via LRU touch-on-read. The internal runner caches (`aggregateToolResultPressureWarnings`, `aggregateToolResultRecoveryWarnings`) are backed by this same primitive.

**Regression test:** Both affected test suites pass:

```
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts \
            src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)

```

target.title: fix(compact): make /compact command cancelable via abortEmbeddedAgentRun
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where `/compact` could not be canceled via `/stop`. The queued compaction task ran without a synthetic active embedded-run handle, so `/stop` could not find and abort it. Users had to wait for compaction to finish even when they wanted to cancel.

## Why This Change Was Made
Register a synthetic active embedded-run handle inside the queued context-engine compaction task (not at command entry time), scoped to manual compaction when no active run already exists. Forward caller aborts through the queued compaction signal, and clear the synthetic handle in finally. Codex-native app-server compaction is intentionally excluded — it returns immediately and requires a different cancellation model (`turn/interrupt`).

## User Impact
Users can now `/stop` a running `/compact` command. The compaction is cancelled and the session state is not corrupted.

## Evidence

All proof on current head `7cb7d21cb7`, freshly rebased on latest `main` (was 381 commits behind). The earlier `delegate.ts` abort-forward hunk is **dropped** — that forwarding is now upstream on `main` via #89886, so this PR is now just the manual-compaction active-run registration (`compact.queued.ts`) plus the drain-timeout guard (`commands-compact.ts`); the abort chain still completes through `main`'s delegate.

### Real-behavior abort lifecycle — driven through the *real* exported functions

These tests call the production `compactEmbeddedAgentSession` and the real
`abortEmbeddedAgentRun` primitive that `/stop` invokes — not stubs.

**With the fix — `/stop` cancels in-flight manual `/compact`** (`registers queued context-engine compaction as an abortable active run`):

1. manual `/compact` enters the queued task → `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(sessionId)` becomes `true` (synthetic handle registered)
2. `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId)` (the exact `/stop` primitive) returns `true`
3. the queued compaction's `abortSignal.aborted` flips to `true` → compaction returns `ok:false`
4. after the task settles, `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(sessionId)` is `false` (handle cleared in `finally`)

**Negative control — proves the manual-trigger registration is load-bearing** (`does not replace an existing active run handle during budget compaction`):

- a non-manual (budget) compaction does **not** register the synthetic handle
- `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId)` aborts the *existing* run handle but the compaction `abortSignal.aborted` stays `false` — i.e. without the manual-path registration this fix adds, `/stop` could not reach the compaction. This reproduces the pre-fix behavior.

**Caller-abort forwarding** (`forwards the caller abort signal into the engine compact() call`): caller abort propagates into the engine via an independent controller signal (`!==` caller signal).

```

```

### What was NOT tested

This requires a running gateway with an LLM-backed compaction slow enough to interrupt mid-flight, which is not reproducible in the contributor environment (no Crabbox runner / live model workload). The abort chain it would exercise — `command → runtime.abortEmbeddedAgentRun → queued task signal → engine.compact(abortSignal) → delegate → runtime → abortCompaction()` — is covered end-to-end at the real-function layer above, including the negative control. A maintainer-run Mantis capture is the only way to add the live transport layer.

The runtime cancellation lifecycle this PR adds is proven end-to-end at the **real-function** layer (see Evidence): the production `compactEmbeddedAgentSession`, the real `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` primitive that `/stop` invokes, the in-flight `engine.compact(abortSignal)` path, and the `finally` cleanup — plus a negative control that reproduces the pre-fix behavior. The transport layer above the proven code is a thin `command → runtime.abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId)` call. Two maintainer-owned ways forward:

target.title: fix: cancel Android link preview calls
target.body:
Closes #101810

AI-assisted with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android chat link previews could keep background network work alive after the preview coroutine was cancelled, such as when users scroll away from a preview or leave the chat screen while metadata or image fetches are still in flight.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android link preview fetcher now executes OkHttp calls through a cancellable coroutine bridge that maps coroutine cancellation to `Call.cancel()`. The same cancellation path is kept active through response body reads, so both metadata and image preview fetches stop promptly without changing the existing wall-clock deadline.

## User Impact

Android users can cancel or leave link preview loading without stranding slow preview downloads on background work. Metadata and image preview behavior remains unchanged for successful fetches, redirects, content-type checks, and cache behavior.

## Evidence

- `JAVA_HOME=/Users/nianjiu/.gradle/jdks/eclipse_adoptium-21-aarch64-os_x.2/jdk-21.0.7+6/Contents/Home pnpm android:test --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatLinkPreviewTest --rerun-tasks` passed: 33 executed tasks, including forced `ChatLinkPreviewTest` execution.

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited `sessionUpdate` property (from prototype pollution or a library mixin) would match and cause the real ACP notification to be silently dropped.

`Object.hasOwn()` is the correct semantic for own-property checks — it only matches properties directly on the object, not inherited ones.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` — a 1-line semantic change from prototype-chain lookup to own-property check.

`Object.hasOwn` is available in Node.js 16.9+ (the project requires Node >= 22).

## Evidence

### Prototype-chain injection proof

```
=== Prototype-chain injection proof ===

Object has own property "agent_message_chunk": true
Object inherits "sessionUpdate" from prototype: true
Object.hasOwn("sessionUpdate"): false

--- Before fix (in operator) ---
  BLOCKED: sessionUpdate matched (inherited!)
  ✗ BUG: inherited property blocks real notification

--- After fix (Object.hasOwn) ---
  PASS: no own sessionUpdate
  ✓ CORRECT: ignores inherited property

✅ Fix confirmed: Object.hasOwn prevents prototype-chain interference
```

Run with: `node proof-object-hasown.ts`

### Vitest

```
pnpm test src/acp/client.test.ts
  printSessionUpdate
    ✓ skips update objects without own sessionUpdate property
    ✓ skips update objects where sessionUpdate is inherited from prototype
    ✓ processes own sessionUpdate notifications
```

| `src/acp/client.ts` | 1 line: `in` → `Object.hasOwn` |
| `src/acp/client.test.ts` | +3 test cases covering own-property, inherited, and normal paths |

target.title: fix(mattermost): inherit thread context in message tool send action
target.body:
## Problem

When the agent uses the `message` tool to send a proactive message (without an explicit `replyTo`) from a Mattermost thread-scoped session, the message lands at the channel root instead of the current thread.

## Root Cause

Two issues:

1. The Mattermost plugin did not implement `threading.buildToolContext`, so the message tool never received `currentThreadTs` or `replyToMode` from the active session. The generic fallback only supplied `currentChannelId` — thread context was never propagated.

2. `context.To` is `channel:<id>` format from monitor.ts, but there is a potential mismatch if any intermediate layer adds the `mattermost:` prefix. The fix strips any such prefix defensively before storing as `currentChannelId`.

## Fix

### 1. Add `threading.buildToolContext` to the Mattermost plugin

Supplies the message tool with:
- `currentChannelId` — platform prefix stripped defensively (`.replace(/^mattermost:/i, "")`) for correct comparison
- `currentThreadTs` — from `MessageThreadId` or `ReplyToId`
- `replyToMode` — resolved from account config, with `off→all` promotion when already inside a thread (mirrors `extensions/slack/src/threading-tool-context.ts`)
- `hasRepliedRef` — passed through

### 2. Inherit thread context in `handleAction` send path

`replyToId` falls back to `toolContext.currentThreadTs` with guards:
- Both `to` and `currentChannelId` normalized via `normalizeMattermostMessagingTarget` before comparison
- `replyToMode` gate: `all` always inherits; `first` inherits only with explicit `hasRepliedRef` present and false (absent ref fails-closed); `off` + existing thread promoted to `all`
- `hasRepliedRef.value` flipped to `true` after any threaded send (implicit or explicit) under `replyToMode=first`

Explicit `replyTo` always takes precedence.

## Tests

9 unit test cases in `channel.test.ts` covering all guard branches and edge cases.

## How to test

1. Configure Mattermost with `replyToMode: "all"`
2. Start a conversation in a channel thread
3. Have the agent call `message(action="send", channel="mattermost", message="...")` **without specifying `replyTo` or `target`** (letting routing decide implicitly)
4. Before: message appears at channel root
5. After: message appears in the current thread

A good reproduction is the cron/heartbeat wake case: set a cron job that wakes a thread-scoped session and has the agent send a message — before this fix the reply would land as a DM or channel root.

## Note on `.github/workflows/preflight.yml`

This file is fork-specific CI scaffolding that lives in the teconomix/openclaw fork. It is not included in this PR's diff (the PR diff covers only `channel.ts` and `channel.test.ts`).

## Rebased on current main (2026-03-25)

Previously based on a stale merge base. Rebased cleanly onto upstream/main as a single commit.

Closes #45082

target.title: fix: same-session inferred commitments can be starved indefinitely when a normal HEARTBEAT.md...
target.body:
## Summary

Found one regression risk: same-session inferred commitments can be starved indefinitely when a normal `HEARTBEAT.md` task is due on every heartbeat tick.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Medium: recurring due heartbeat tasks can prevent same-session commitments from ever delivering** (regression)
  - File: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`
  - Evidence: `firstDueCommitment` is now only selected when `dueHeartbeatTasks.length === 0` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`). When any task is due, `resolveHeartbeatRunPrompt` returns the task prompt with `hasDueCommitments: false` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:870`), so `dueCommitmentIds` is empty and the commitment is neither attempted nor delivered. The scheduler’s follow-up pass explicitly skips the default session key (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1866`), so same-session commitments depend on a later default heartbeat run with no due tasks. For a documented/common setup like `heartbeat.every: "5m"` and a `tasks:` entry with `interval: 5m`, `isTaskDue` is true again on every cadence tick because it uses `nowMs - lastRunMs >= intervalMs` (`src/auto-reply/heartbeat.ts:288`). The new test covers the first half of this state by asserting the due commitment stays `pending` with `attempts...
  - Impact: users with opt-in inferred commitments and an every-heartbeat task can stop receiving natural follow-up check-ins for that session until the commitment expires, despite docs saying due commitments are delivered through heartbeat for the same agent/channel scope.
  - Suggested fix: keep task turns tool-capable, but process same-session commitments in a separate no-tools turn after the task run, or add a commitment-only wake/path that bypasses task selection without mixing untrusted commitment metadata into the tool-capable task prompt.

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.
